```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(nlme)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

load("WtLoss.RData")
```


# part a

```{r}
str(wtloss)

wtloss$diet <- factor(wtloss$diet, levels = c(0, 1, 2))
contrasts(wtloss$diet) <- contr.treatment(
  levels(wtloss$diet),
  base = 1
)

wtloss$id <- factor(wtloss$id)
wtloss <- wtloss[order(wtloss$id, wtloss$time), ]
```


```{r}
# Model (i): random intercept
fit_ri <- lme(
  fixed = weight ~ diet * time,
  random = ~ 1 | id,
  data = wtloss,
  method = "REML"
)


# Model (ii): correlated random intercept and time slope
fit_ris <- lme(
  fixed = weight ~ diet * time,
  random = ~ 1 + time | id,
  data = wtloss,
  method = "REML"
)
```


```{r}
summary(fit_ri)
summary(fit_ris)

VarCorr(fit_ri)
VarCorr(fit_ris)

intervals(fit_ri, which = "fixed")
intervals(fit_ris, which = "fixed")


# Random-effects covariance and correlation matrices
G_ris <- as.matrix(
  getVarCov(fit_ris, type = "random.effects")
)

G_ris
cov2cor(G_ris)

# Residual variance
sigma(fit_ris)^2
```

```{r q1a-table, echo=FALSE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, comment=NA}
terms <- c(
  "(Intercept)", "diet1", "diet2",
  "time", "diet1:time", "diet2:time"
)

labels <- c(
  "Baseline mean: diet 0",
  "Baseline difference: diet 1 vs 0",
  "Baseline difference: diet 2 vs 0",
  "Monthly change: diet 0",
  "Slope difference: diet 1 vs 0",
  "Slope difference: diet 2 vs 0"
)

extract_fixed <- function(fit) {
  tt <- summary(fit)$tTable[terms, , drop = FALSE]
  ci <- intervals(fit, which = "fixed")$fixed[
    terms, , drop = FALSE
  ]

  data.frame(
    estimate = sprintf(
      "%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)",
      tt[, "Value"], ci[, "lower"], ci[, "upper"]
    ),
    p = ifelse(
      tt[, "p-value"] < 0.001,
      "<0.001",
      sprintf("%.3f", tt[, "p-value"])
    )
  )
}

ri <- extract_fixed(fit_ri)
ris <- extract_fixed(fit_ris)

G_ri <- as.matrix(
  getVarCov(fit_ri, type = "random.effects")
)
G_ris <- as.matrix(
  getVarCov(fit_ris, type = "random.effects")
)

fixed_rows <- data.frame(
  Parameter = labels,
  RI = ri$estimate,
  RI_p = ri$p,
  RIS = ris$estimate,
  RIS_p = ris$p
)

random_rows <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c(
    "Random-intercept variance",
    "Random-slope variance",
    "Intercept-slope covariance",
    "Intercept-slope correlation",
    "Residual variance"
  ),
  RI = c(
    sprintf("%.4f", G_ri[1, 1]),
    rep("--", 3),
    sprintf("%.4f", sigma(fit_ri)^2)
  ),
  RI_p = "",
  RIS = sprintf(
    "%.4f",
    c(
      G_ris[1, 1],
      G_ris[2, 2],
      G_ris[1, 2],
      cov2cor(G_ris)[1, 2],
      sigma(fit_ris)^2
    )
  ),
  RIS_p = ""
)

table_data <- rbind(fixed_rows, random_rows)
is_latex <- knitr::is_latex_output()

notes <- paste(
  "Both models were fitted by REML using 997 observations from 120 patients.",
  "Time is in months; month 0 is baseline.",
  "Diet 0 is the reference group: baseline counseling only;",
  "diet 1: counseling at all visits;",
  "diet 2: counseling at all visits plus free exercise-facility access.",
  "Fixed effects are estimates (95% CIs) with model-based t-test p values.",
  "Variance components and the correlation are point estimates only.",
  "A dash indicates a parameter absent from model (i).",
  "Weight is reported in the original, unspecified measurement units."
)

args <- list(
  x = table_data,
  format = if (is_latex) "latex" else "html",
  caption = "Linear mixed-effects models of weight over time.",
  col.names = c(
    "Parameter",
    "Estimate (95% CI)", "p value",
    "Estimate (95% CI)", "p value"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)

if (is_latex) args$booktabs <- TRUE

tab_q1a <- do.call(knitr::kable, args) |>
  add_header_above(
    c(
      " " = 1,
      "Random intercept" = 2,
      "Random intercept and slope" = 2
    )
  ) |>
  pack_rows("Fixed effects", 1, 6) |>
  pack_rows("Variance components", 7, 11)

if (is_latex) {
  tab_q1a <- tab_q1a |>
    column_spec(1, width = "4.2cm") |>
    kable_styling(
      latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down"),
      font_size = 9
    )
} else {
  tab_q1a <- tab_q1a |>
    column_spec(1, width = "260px") |>
    kable_styling(
      full_width = FALSE,
      position = "center"
    )
}

tab_q1a <- tab_q1a |>
  footnote(
    general = notes,
    general_title = "Notes: ",
    footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
    threeparttable = is_latex,
    fixed_small_size = TRUE
  )

tab_q1a
```


\noindent\textbf{Interpretation of model (ii).}

Let $D_{1k}=I(\mathrm{diet}_k=1)$ and
$D_{2k}=I(\mathrm{diet}_k=2)$. The model is
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_{ki} ={}&
\beta_0^*+\beta_1^*D_{1k}+\beta_2^*D_{2k}
+\beta_3^*t_{ki}
+\beta_4^*D_{1k}t_{ki}
+\beta_5^*D_{2k}t_{ki}\\
&+\gamma_{0k}+\gamma_{1k}t_{ki}+\epsilon_{ki},
\end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\gamma_{0k}\\
\gamma_{1k}
\end{pmatrix}
\sim N\left[
\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\end{pmatrix},
G
\right],
\qquad
\epsilon_{ki}\sim N(0,\sigma_\epsilon^2).
\]
Random effects and residual errors are independent, and
patients are independent of one another.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Fixed effects.}

\begin{itemize}
\item $\widehat{\beta}_0^*=250.992$:
The estimated baseline mean weight in diet 0 was
250.992 weight units
(95\% CI: 249.979, 252.004).

\item $\widehat{\beta}_1^*=-0.697$:
At baseline, patients in diet 1 weighed an estimated
0.697 units less than those in diet 0
(95\% CI for the difference: $-2.141$, $0.748$;
$p=0.341$).

\item $\widehat{\beta}_2^*=-2.687$:
At baseline, patients in diet 2 weighed an estimated
2.687 units less than those in diet 0
(95\% CI for the difference: $-4.132$, $-1.243$;
$p<0.001$).

\item $\widehat{\beta}_3^*=0.019$:
Estimated mean weight in diet 0 increased by
0.019 units per month
(95\% CI: $-0.053$, $0.091$; $p=0.607$).
There was insufficient evidence of a nonzero linear
change in this group.

\item $\widehat{\beta}_4^*=-0.102$:
Monthly weight change in diet 1 was
0.102 units lower than in diet 0
(95\% CI for the difference: $-0.201$, $-0.003$;
$p=0.044$).
The estimated slope in diet 1 was
\[
\widehat{\beta}_3^*+\widehat{\beta}_4^*
=-0.083
\]
weight units per month.

\item $\widehat{\beta}_5^*=-0.491$:
Monthly weight change in diet 2 was
0.491 units lower than in diet 0
(95\% CI for the difference: $-0.590$, $-0.393$;
$p<0.001$).
The estimated slope in diet 2 was
\[
\widehat{\beta}_3^*+\widehat{\beta}_5^*
=-0.472
\]
weight units per month.
\end{itemize}

The treatment-specific slopes were calculated before
rounding. They imply estimated average weight losses
of 0.083 and 0.472 units per month in diets 1 and 2,
respectively.

The interaction coefficients represent differences
between slopes. Their $p$ values test these differences
relative to diet 0, rather than testing whether each
treatment group's own slope equals zero.

Because the model uses an identity link and mean-zero
random effects, the fixed-effect trajectories also
describe population mean trajectories within each
treatment group. Individual trajectories vary around
these means through the random intercept and slope.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Variance components.}

The estimated random-effects covariance matrix was
\[
\widehat{G}=
\begin{pmatrix}
10.2416 & -0.2099\\
-0.2099 & 0.0262
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\widehat{\sigma}_\epsilon^2=1.0011.
\]

\begin{itemize}
\item
The random-intercept variance was 10.2416,
corresponding to a standard deviation of
3.200 weight units.
It describes between-patient variation in underlying
baseline weight around the treatment-specific
baseline means.

\item
The random-slope variance was 0.0262,
corresponding to a standard deviation of
0.162 weight units per month.
It describes between-patient variation in underlying
monthly weight change around the treatment-specific
mean slopes.

\item
The intercept--slope covariance was $-0.2099$,
with a correlation of $-0.405$.
Within a treatment group, patients whose underlying
baseline weight was above the group mean tended
to have lower, more negative weight-change slopes,
indicating a greater tendency toward weight loss.

\item
The residual variance was 1.0011,
corresponding to a standard deviation of
1.001 weight units.
It describes variation in observed weights around
each patient's fitted trajectory after accounting
for the fixed and random effects.
\end{itemize}

The intercept and residual variances have units of
squared weight units; the slope variance has units
of squared weight units per month squared; and
the intercept--slope covariance has units of squared
weight units per month. The correlation is dimensionless.
